01 / ONE SOURCE OF TRUTH

The backend owns the rules.

Prices, availability, permissions, order transitions, campaign benefits, and payment state are decided and persisted by the API.

02 / CONNECTED THROUGH CONTRACTS

Three apps. Shared contracts.

Customer, provider, and admin apps exchange data through backend APIs. Each has its own interface and responsibility.

03 / SEPARATE RESPONSIBILITIES

Requests, events, and sessions.

HTTP handles business actions. RabbitMQ carries asynchronous work. Socket.IO handles live conversations on the retained chat runtime.

New API and worker share events_queue_release_20261014_1
Original consumer and its queue remain retained

Runtime services are Docker Swarm services on a DigitalOcean Droplet. MongoDB and DigitalOcean Spaces are accessed through configured connections; the inspected sources do not establish the database's physical hosting provider.

The runtime distinctions that matter

Chat stays on the legacy backend. Current API candidates bridge chat HTTP to the retained owner. Nginx keeps Socket.IO traffic with that owner; ordinary jobs remain there too.

API and worker are separate processes. The new release uses a dedicated queue. The old consumer and queue are still retained; a queue is not a database or a real-time socket server.

Redis is optional support in source. The shared Socket.IO Redis adapter is implemented for future multi-instance chat. The documented production bootstrap keeps legacy chat rather than enabling that design.

Flutter / Dart → Android and iOS appsFlutter build → static browser assets served by NginxNestJS 8 / TypeScript → Node.js 20 container buildDocker Swarm + CapRover → services, routing and release infrastructureMongoDB + Mongoose → durable business records and transactionsRabbitMQ → event transport; consumer → delivery handlers and auto-bids
